alignments.note: `כַּאֲשֶׁר` → *as* is fused under rule 30 and headed on the opening morpheme by rule 23's explicit ruling.
Existential `אֵין` heads on the negation word (rule 50); its copula is absorbed into the ASV's finite 'knowest not'.
Suffix on `אֵין` realized by the subject pronoun *thou* (rule 50).
Participial predicate rendered by the finite *knowest*.
Interrogative predicate of the verbless clause; the construction-supplied copula joins it, exactly as rule 20 gives *is* to `מִי` in 'What man is this'.
Construct noun with the supplied *the*, the rectum's own article being written before its own word (rule 29).
Article on the rectum takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29's arthrous case).
Rectum with the chain's relational *of* (rule 19), headed on the noun.

No conjunction morpheme stands in this clause, so the coordinating *nor* answers to nothing and is added under rule 14's closing sentence; the ASV's italic corroborates it. Competing reading: a second realization of `אֵין` distributed over the coordinated phrase under rule 25, but that rule governs the ASV rewriting the same word, and *nor* additionally supplies a coordination no morpheme licenses.
The comparative `כְּ` of 'as the bones' is recast as the manner interrogative *how* continuing 'thou knowest not what ... nor how ...'; that word is what the ASV spends on this preposition.
Noun with its supplied *the*, no article morpheme being present (rule 15).
The Hebrew phrase has no verb; the ASV supplies the whole lexical predicate 'do grow', which is added under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause. Both italics corroborate.
`בְּ` rendered *in*.
Construct noun with a supplied *the*, no article morpheme standing on it.

Substantival article takes the supplied pronoun 'her that' and heads on the pronoun (rule 41); the chain's relational *of* falls in the rectum's unit under rule 19. Competing reading: attaching *of* to the adjective's unit instead, which would make that unit discontinuous for no gain.
The adjective 'full' is rendered idiomatically 'is with child', the copula joining it under rules 20 and 41; headed on the content word *child*.
`כָּכָה` rendered by the two-word adverb 'even so', headed on *so*.
Negative.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun.
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
Construct noun; the phrase's single *the* is fronted from the rectum's article under rule 29.
Article on the rectum: the ASV renders the rectum anarthrously ('of God'), so the written *the* is fronted to the phrase's left edge and belongs to this morpheme (rule 29).
Rectum with the chain's *of* (rule 19).
Relative rendered *who*.
Finite verb.
Object marker with no English of its own.
Article: the ASV writes a bare *all* and no *the* for the phrase, so the article is unrepresented under rule 29.
`כֹּל` rendered *all*.

review_notes: The three ASV italics (*nor*, *do*, *grow*) all fall where no morpheme licenses the English, so each is added; the comparative `כְּ` keeps the non-italic *how*.

`מַעֲשֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים` is an anarthrous-rectum chain, so its written *the* is fronted to the article under rule 29, while `דֶּרֶךְ הָרוּחַ` writes a *the* before each word and each morpheme takes the one before its own.
